run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not identify which service handled request REQ-EU-8K4M2 or what failed it: the two sources that carry request-level telemetry for this target (Jaeger traces and Prometheus metrics) failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call, and the Elasticsearch indices contain only uniform synthetic background records (162 in-window documents, all level INFO, message "Request completed successfully", response_time_ms 150 in every region including eu-west). Within the readable evidence the otel-demo workloads were running and ready and their application logs show successful traffic (checkout PlaceOrder -> payment -> email sequences at 08:42-08:48, ad requests at 08:45-08:48); the only error logs found are startup-era connection/DNS failures around the stack starts at 2026-11-20T16:32-16:33 and 2026-11-21T04:23-04:24, plus one previous-instance nginx error on the Prometheus read proxy. A mass container termination across all otel-demo pods at 2026-11-21T04:23:42 (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) is a change in the window whose trigger I could not establish. No root cause is asserted.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch store holds 1620 indices, all named app-185-geo-<region>-<service>-2024.01.xx. In the 40-row slice of the index list I read, every index shows docs.count 1 and 8-8.1kb store size except app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, which shows docs.count 2 and 12kb.

Across all 1620 indices, the 24h window 2026-11-20T08:49:31Z-2026-11-21T08:49:31Z contains 162 documents (one per region/service pair), all of level INFO, all with the single response_time_ms value 150; the region buckets ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, eu-west, us-east and us-west each contain 27 documents with max and average response_time_ms 150.

All 22 otel-demo pods were Running and ready; each application container shows restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated reason Unknown, exitCode 255, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (for example frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n).
All 25 deployments in the cluster report 1 of 1 replicas ready, including every otel-demo service and the jaeger, prometheus, otel-collector and prometheus-readonly-proxy deployments.

The frontend previous container instance logged gRPC error code 14 UNAVAILABLE, 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080', at 2026-11-20T16:33:30Z and 2026-11-20T16:33:42Z; 10.96.220.188 is the ClusterIP of the otel-demo cart Service.

The cart container's previous instance started at 2026-11-20T16:33:37Z, i.e. after the frontend's 16:33:30Z connection refusal to the cart ClusterIP, so that refusal precedes cart becoming available and coincides with the stack's 16:32-16:33 startup.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod shows restartCount 3, and its previous nginx instance logged 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22' at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z; the pod's nginx configuration is mounted from a Secret that cannot be read.

The jaeger container (jaeger-698d849b7b-sjz9c) restarted and its current instance logged 'Query server started' with http_addr [::]:16686 and grpc_addr [::]:16685 at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z; this all-in-one Jaeger keeps traces in memory, so the restart reset its trace store.

The current Prometheus server instance was ingesting continuously: its log shows repeated WARN 'Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars' (num_dropped 4-10) from 2026-11-21T08:19:48Z through 2026-11-21T08:48:49Z.

Prometheus is configured with the alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh: checkout PlaceOrder server spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR divided by all such spans over 5m > 0.5, for 2m, severity critical.

checkout application logs at 08:42-08:48Z show repeated successful sequences: '[PlaceOrder] user_id=...', then 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' about 18-20 ms later, then 'order confirmation email sent to ...' about 9 ms after payment (for example 08:48:45.645 -> 08:48:45.665 -> 08:48:45.674).

The ad service served targeted and non-targeted ad requests between 2026-11-21T08:45:03Z and 08:48:21Z with trace ids recorded, and the newest ad log line matching error|fail|deadline|timeout|unavailable|refused|slow that the query returned was at 2026-11-21T04:24:25Z (startup flagd/otel-collector name-resolution failures).

The flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) defines the fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant "off".
The load-generator deployment runs with LOCUST_USERS=2, LOCUST_SPAWN_RATE=1, LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080 and LOCUST_BROWSER_TRAFFIC_ENABLED=false, and carries no region/EU setting.

Alertmanager's window log lines matching Checkout|alert|firing|resolved were six startup/configuration lines between 2026-11-20T16:33:40Z and 2026-11-21T04:23:47Z; no alert-receipt or notification line was among them.

The latency/error evidence that would identify the service behind REQ-EU-8K4M2 sits in Jaeger spans (tagged with the request id) and Prometheus latency series, both of which could not be queried, so the affected service cannot be named from this Run.

The extra document in app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 (docs.count 2 versus 1 elsewhere) might be a request-level error record mentioning REQ-EU-8K4M2 in the eu-west region, but both of that index's documents fall outside the readable window and their content could not be read, so this remains unverified.

That a flagd fault-injection flag was active for a specific service at the time of the complaint: every documented flag in demo.flagd.json has defaultVariant "off"; this only reflects the config value read now and not its history.

That an otel-demo service pod was crash-looping or not ready during the window: all otel-demo pods were Running and ready and each application container had restartCount 1, a single mass termination at 04:23:42Z rather than repeated restarts.

In the readable window the Elasticsearch geo-log dataset shows no slow responses: all 162 documents, including all 27 eu-west documents, are INFO with response_time_ms 150, identical to the other five regions.

gaps: Jaeger was not queryable: traces_list_services, traces_search (frontend, checkout), traces_search_by_tags (frontend, request.id="REQ-EU-8K4M2"), traces_query_trace_by_id and traces_list_operations all returned status=error, reason=SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, tag or trace for REQ-EU-8K4M2 was obtained and the calling/serving service cannot be identified from traces.

Prometheus was not queryable: get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned status=error, reason=SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so latency histograms, error ratios and trace-derived call metrics could not be read.

The Elasticsearch query '"REQ-EU-8K4M2"' over all 1620 indices in the 24h window returned 0 documents; ES only returns documents whose @timestamp lies inside the window, 1458 of 1620 indices had no document in the window, and documents outside the window (including the two documents of app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05) cannot be read with this tool, so the request id is unverified rather than proven absent.

The trigger of the mass container termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, all otel-demo pods) is unknown; the only events returned in the window were app-223 Pod/Deployment/ReplicaSet/Endpoints events between 08:28Z and 08:49Z, and events expire, so no node/kubelet event explains it.

Pod logs only cover the previous container instance and the current one; the previous instances end around 04:07Z and the current ones start 04:23Z, and no log exists for otel-demo before 2026-11-20T16:32Z, so any earlier request activity is unknown.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx configuration is mounted from a Secret that cannot be read, so the upstream definition that produced 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' could not be inspected and the current proxy behaviour for reader traffic is unverified.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so the history of flagd flag values and ConfigMap edits around the incident cannot be established.

No source reports a region attribute inside the otel-demo stack (frontend, load-generator and collector configurations carry no region/EU setting), so it is unverified how the customer's 'Europe' maps to any service in this target.
The frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, currency and quote containers produced no log lines in the sampled windows, so their request-level health during the complaint could not be assessed.
next_steps: Restore or verify the Jaeger query path (jaeger-query service 16686/16685) and the Prometheus read path (prometheus-readonly-proxy after its upstream 'prometheus:9090' resolution failure), then re-run a trace search for the request id tag and inspect the slowest span's service and operation.

Once metrics are readable, compare per-service latency histograms (rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) across the window to confirm which service's latency deviates and whether it is latency-only.

Obtain access to the underlying Elasticsearch documents for app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 (both documents lie outside the tool's time window) to check whether they contain the REQ-EU-8K4M2 record, and widen the searchable time range.
Ask the customer for the exact URL/page and timestamp behind REQ-EU-8K4M2 and confirm how their 'Europe' region maps to this deployment, since the otel-demo stack has no region attribute.

Review node/containerd logs for the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z mass restart (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) to determine whether it was a node event and whether it displaced evidence (Jaeger in-memory traces, Prometheus data) from before that time.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
